utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen; good morning to the technical booth and the interpreters; good morning to the legal assistants and registrar, the audience, the Prosecution, the Defence counsel. They're all there. Good morning to the accused. We're going to take up where we left off yesterday and that is the continuation of the cross-examination of Witness J. I'm going to ask the usher to lower the blinds to permit the witness to enter, and we shall begin straight after that. I think that it is Mr. Stojanovic's and Mr. Masic's turn for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes. May we take our seats before the witness enters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please do to speed up matters, because we're lagging behind anyway. But it seems to be warmer in the courtroom here today. There were some technical problems, but I think we'll heat up the room with our work. I have already asked the registrar to inquire as to what is going on, otherwise, there will be a sauna in here and that's not why we're here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness J. Can you hear me? Can you hear me, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to check the technical equipment. We spoke about a sauna a moment ago, but let us add that when you're in a sauna, you have to go out every half hour for a cold shower. But anyway, Witness, I hope that you have had a good rest and that you are fresh and ready to answer the questions put to you by Defence counsel. Mr. Stojanovic, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness J. I think that you are highly qualified, but I have to address you in that way. My name is Stojanovic. I am a lawyer from Belgrade. And my colleague Simo Tosic make up the Defence counsel of Mr. Zoran Zigic. Yesterday, my learned colleagues Mr. O'Sullivan and Mr. Krstan Simic showed you your witness statements which were given sometime in 1995 to the representatives of the Tribunal. Do you remember that taking place yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read you a portion of the text which refers to Zoran Zigic, one of the accused. It is on page 16 of your statement of the English text and the B/C/S text, both on page 16. "I saw him coming and going from the camp by car. I saw him talking to a guard. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you state that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now dwell on that statement for a moment. Can you explain to us where Mr. Zigic parked his car on that particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You showed us his position yesterday and the position of certain other individuals who were there. Can you tell us whether it was close to the spot which you indicated yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He parked his car between the "white house" and the pista, but as far as I remember at this point in time, it was closer to the "white house."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that still the pista?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I call that whole space from in front of the restaurant right up to the grassy patch, I refer to that as the pista. That is according to the image that is in my mind at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that when getting out of the car, he moved in your direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He -- as I said yesterday, he moved between the pista and the "white house," in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I am talking about his movements after he got out of the car.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, towards the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was he driving the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. I don't know. I didn't pay detailed attention to that, nor was I allowed to look. I don't know if he drove the car or not. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any other individuals in the car with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice any.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can I take that to mean that he was alone in the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know. I can't claim that now, neither could I claim that previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us the make of the car? What type of car was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume, although I'm not quite sure, that it was a Mercedes, but I'm not quite sure. I say that once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But it was a passenger car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't happen to remember the colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for sure, perhaps it was sort of yellowish.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: One of your answers yesterday was along these lines. Perhaps I'll -- let me try and formulate that question better. Of the prisoners, was there nobody on the pista at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there was anybody there, no. And I stated that yesterday, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know which guard he talked to, if you remember? You said that he talked to a guard, but do you remember which one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When I made my statement the first time, I did not identify the guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. You said you didn't know, but I have to ask you that question and with a little more detail. Do you not know because you didn't know the guard, or don't you know because you were not able to see the guard properly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps I saw him, perhaps not. I couldn't say with any precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the guard? Never mind the name, did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I probably saw him in the camp. I got to know most of them in the camp during the time that I spent in the camp, but personally, I can't say that I actually knew him. Had I knew him personally, I would probably be able to tell you his identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojanovic, I think you're going around in circles. Let's move on and ask other questions. You are becoming argumentative with the witness once again. The witness said she saw a guard. Now you're going around in circles and saying, "Does that mean you saw him, you didn't see him?" You see the point I'm trying to make, Mr. Stojanovic. Please move ahead; otherwise, we'll be going round and round in circles.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Zigic called out certain persons by name. Apart from the people you enumerated, did he ask for other males as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did, yes, and I forgot to state that. I'm not quite sure, but I think it was Emir Beganovic, nicknamed Braco.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he call out any women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear him do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You described what he looked like, his uniform and his cap. Did you notice any other -- anything else on him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you happen to notice a bandage of any kind on his body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, nor could I stare at him for that long.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The day before yesterday you said that at the time you asked Adnan Ado who the man was. Why did you ask Mr. Ado that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to check to make sure whether what I thought was correct, and he said, "That's Zigic. I'm sure you know him." And he said -- and I said, "Ah, it can't be him." I said I'm afraid; he does a lot of shouting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Witness. That will do. You have given me an answer to my question. We heard yesterday that, after coming back from the lavatory, you saw Zigic standing in front of the "white house." How long did you watch him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it for a minute, or ten minutes perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be specific. I can't tell you how long it lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the occasion, was Zigic standing in front of the "white house" alone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I saw him clearly, but as to the rest, I wasn't paying that much attention. There were probably some guards standing around, but I did see him standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now move on to the events in Trnopolje. When did you arrive in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived in Trnopolje, as I already stated, on the 3rd of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what time of day it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was before noon when we were -- our names were called out, and it took us perhaps an hour to reach Trnopolje. I'm not quite sure. First of all, the roll call was taken. Then we boarded the bus, and that took some time. We had to go out in front of the administration building to board the bus. Now, how long all that could have lasted, I really don't know. I was so happy to be leaving. I thought I was leaving somewhere where it would be better and that I might survive, so I didn't pay too much attention to the time all this took. But I knew -- I do know that it was all before noon on the 3rd of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we take it that you arrived there at around noon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. It could have been in the afternoon as well because the whole procedure of getting out of the restaurant, being called out, being loaded into the bus, the guards assigned to escort us, I really can't say how long all that lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When did you leave Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left Trnopolje on the 8th of August of that same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When was that during the day? Can you tell us the time of day that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't quite remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it in the morning, in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it might have been 12.00, after 12.00. But I arrived into the town, the town of Prijedor, sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When did you see Zigic in Trnopolje? Can you tell us something more precise, be more specific about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you what day it was exactly, but it was -- when I was in Trnopolje, I saw him with my own eyes. I saw Zigic, and that is what I stated. He arrived in Trnopolje, and once again --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You've already described those events. I just have some specific questions to ask you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what time of day it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was daytime, daylight.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you be more specific and tell us whether it was the morning or the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, I can't. I'm not going to say anything that I'm not absolutely sure about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that he came by car and that he was looking for a man called Edin Ganic. Do you happen to know which car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was a Golf, metallic colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you hear his voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him and I heard him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Unless I'm wrong, I think you said that you were inside.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was at the entrance of the room, but it was all open.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you recount that event to the OTP during your interview in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember whether I did or did not. I just can't remember at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you tell the Prosecution about Zigic's calling out women and verbally abusing them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I spoke about it, but I remember that incident very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you make a request to leave? I think that the Prosecution supplied a document to that effect in evidence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to receive that permit to leave; otherwise, I was not able to leave the town and move to free territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Unless I'm wrong, the permit was granted you. You were granted permission and that the permission was signed by a man called Slavko Budimir; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you write that request to leave yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't write anything. I went there with a friend of mine, a girlfriend of mine, a Serb lady, and I asked her to speed matters up, to help me receive the permit. I didn't write anything. I went into an office with her, and I received the permit without any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean you made an oral request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I asked orally, and they said that I had to leave all my property behind and that that was the condition upon which I would receive a permit to leave town. And I said, "That's okay. I'll allow you that, and just give me the paper so I can leave town," because I couldn't have left town without that piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The facts contained in that permit, are they truthful with respect to your request? I don't mean the motives for your wishing to leave but the process of leaving what was called at the time the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you make -- what do you mean? I don't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the problem. The Prosecution has already shown this document, and it was Exhibit D3/116A, the Bosnian, Croatian, and Serbian version, and D3/116B in the English language, and it would appear that you tendered this at the 6th of August, which would make it the time you were in Trnopolje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to show the witness the document again which says that [name redacted] tabled a request to leave the country on the 6th of August, and you say you were in Trnpolje until the 8th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the explanation given, could you have a look at your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just have a moment to take out my glasses, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think that I have been given indication that Mr. Stojanovic pronounced the name of the witness. So let us take measures to delete the name because, Mr. Stojanovic, this is a protected witness, so we may not say the name out loud. Is that what you were going to say, Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That's it, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really do apologise for that omission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you know, these are situations which are very difficult to put right once they go wrong. We're going to take all the necessary steps, but once it has been said, it has been said. We cannot say to the public in the public gallery, "Forget what you have just heard." Anyway, please continue, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness J, have you found your way in this document? The explanation part states that the request was tendered on the 6th of August, 1992, asking permission to leave. Can you explain that difference? At that time you said you were in Trnopolje, on the 8th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm seeing this for the first time today. The permit was issued on the 18th of August. I say again --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm just asking you to explain that to us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat. I did not make any written request. The day I went to the office, I received this paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question did not say that you tabled a written request. I just asked you about the request you made.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never tabled a written request.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted), can a request be made both orally and in written form?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't make a written request from Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is precisely why I want to hear an explanation from you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why this omission has been made.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What is the mistake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: The permit was issued on the 18th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I did not ask you that. It says here that your request -- very well. You say it was oral -- was made on the 6th of August. That's what it says. And you state that at that time you were in Trnopolje. Now, what is true there? What is the correct version?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I was in Trnopolje. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The day before yesterday, you told us that you knew Mr. Miroslav Kvocka well from before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That same day, you told us that you know Mr. Mladjo Radic very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not as well as Mr. Kvocka. I knew him by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But you got to know him much better in the camp, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also say that you knew Mr. Drago Prcac before the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a worker of the SUP, as a SUP employee.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you also say that you got to know, in the camp, the accused Kos well and that you remember him because of the fringe he wore?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know which of the accused in this courtroom remains? Which is the other person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd have to get up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, you don't have to identify anybody. Do you know just which the other accused is in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the commander of the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To come to here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. The other person who is in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you explain that to me in greater detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we enumerated four individuals whom you know are the accused and whom you know personally. Now, is there another person in this room who stands accused and who is on trial here today or the day before yesterday? When you completed your identification process, in addition to these four individuals whom you stated that you knew --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm following you. I follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- is there somebody else in this courtroom who is one of the accused?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course there is. Zoran Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid you got me muddled.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness J.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Masic and Mr. Jovan Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you may proceed, Mr. Masic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness J. My name is Dusan Masic. I'm a lawyer from Belgrade, and together with my colleague Mr. Jovan Simic, I'm representing the accused Drago Prcac in this case. To begin with, I should like to ask you whether you knew Drago before you arrived in the camp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: For how long did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him since late 1970s. Approximately since 1978, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: During your examination-in-chief, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Do you know what Drago did before the Omarska camp was set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a crime technician. He was an employee of the former SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Was he working until the camp was set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what he was at that time, whether he had already retired or whether he was still an employee there. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you how many times I would see him, but I saw him often.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: So one could say that you knew Drago Prcac very well, that you knew how he looked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were on very friendly terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: As regards your examination-in-chief, could you tell us whether you told us only about things that you yourself saw, or did you also recount things that you heard from other detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only told you about the things that I experienced.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: I'm actually interested in the things you saw, that you saw directly, that you could observe yourself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that, according to your testimony, Mr. Prcac arrived in the Omarska camp in mid-July? That is what you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: So he was there since mid-July until the 3rd of August. That is when you left the camp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was sometime in mid-July. I cannot tell you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: So that would amount to a period of about 20 days during your stay in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: You testified in chief that you had seen Drago Prcac giving assignments to the guards. When, where, and to which guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you which guards he gave assignments to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the time when he would do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would see him in the morning, at other times of the day as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Did he issue orders to the guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would give them assignments, indicate them what to do. He would motion to them where they were supposed to go in the camp. He would carry some kind of lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: So from 7 or 8.00 in the morning until 7 or 8.00 in the evening, you were in the restaurant, and during that time you could observe things freely; otherwise, you were locked up, and you could only go to the toilet. Does that mean you would see Drago only during the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: You told us you had seen him giving assignments to the guards. Could you describe to us the locations where he would assign the guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would assign them to stand around the restaurant, in the direction of the "white house," the garage, other buildings where detainees were put.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that he was only giving assignments to individual guards and not to the complete shifts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Yesterday in response to a question put to you by one of my learned colleagues that the shifts would be relieved inside the administration building, that is, in the office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes that would take place in the office and sometimes outside the entrance. Near the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that there was not a strict procedure as regards the changeover the guards? Sometimes it would take place inside, sometimes outside; sometimes Meakic would be in charge, sometimes Prcac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to what I could observe, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: We can therefore conclude that it was a chaotical procedure.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Keegan. I know what you're going to say, but please, do say so. Mr. Masic, you cannot draw such conclusions. You should confine yourselves to questions and not draw any conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I'm going to reformulate my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Was the changeover of guards carried in anarchical manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "anarchy."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Masic, if you're going to use such an adjective, it means that you are drawing conclusions. If you're going to ask such a question, it means you are already making judgements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I thought it was a proper question, but I'm going to withdraw it anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Masic, you can ask the witness what was the procedure of the changeover, but you cannot ask the witness if the changeover was carried out in an anarchical manner. You can ask her about the procedure itself and what it looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance, Your Honours. I hope that the witness has heard your question as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: So could you please describe to us the changeover of guards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already spoken about that. New guards would arrive in a group, the old ones would leave, and as I have already said, it took place in front of the entrance to the administration building. Sometimes it would take place on the pista or in the reception office or the administration office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: You told us a while ago that sometimes Meakic and Prcac would give assignments to the guards together; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: You testified that Drago Prcac would very often call out detainees. Where would he do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him around the restaurant, but he was walking around the camp, and he was probably visiting locations where the detainees were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness J, but I want to know where you saw him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was clear enough, I believe. I saw him in front of the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Could you be more specific as to the time and to the individuals he would call out and how often that would take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot tell you that. I don't know about the time, when it took place, and I don't know the names and surnames of people who he called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: How can you therefore claim that you would no longer see the individuals in question in the restaurant? How can you say that if you do not know those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you an endless list of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: No, don't do that. Just give me the names of the people that were called out by Drago Prcac and who were no longer to be seen in the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I cannot tell you that at the moment. You want me to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: No, let me ask you one further question. You left for Trnopolje on the 3rd of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Was it Drago Prcac who called you out on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that Drago Prcac called out the names of the people who were supposed to go to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: How come, since he called out your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't call out several of the women detainees, and they never left the camp. They were not on the list that he was using.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm asking. Was he calling out the names of the people who were leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He called us women in the presence of Zeljko Meakic in the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: So he read out the names from the list in the presence of Zeljko Meakic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. No further questions. I apologise Your Honour, let me ask one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: One last question, Witness J, I apologise. I forgot to ask you one particular thing. Yesterday you told my colleague, Mr. Krstan Simic, (redacted) (redacted). Did you read that article?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw him [sic] yesterday for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: At that time, did you tell the truth to the journalists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always tell the truth, and that is what I told you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: Were there any children in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were young people who were underage at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: You know exactly what I mean by children. I'm asking you about children.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say that there were some people there who were minors. I can give you names of two of them. I can identify two such individuals. There were two underage persons whom I knew personally and whose parents I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: In the article that I mentioned, you state there were many children in the camp. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. Masic. The witness has already said that she is not aware of the contents of the document. You have to bear in mind that there is a journalist between the witness and the public. She has already said that she cannot confirm the words as they were conveyed in the article.

utterances.speaker: MR. MASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That was the reason of my question regarding the contents of the article. Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an interpreter present during the interview as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Masic. Mr. Keegan, do you have any additional questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Witness J, I'd like to ask you a few questions about some of the areas that have been covered in cross-examination. Let's first start with some general background about the witness statement which you gave to the ICTY in February of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could I have the usher hand a copy of the statement to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Now, it indicates this statement was given over a period of two days; is that correct? The 11th and 14th of February, I believe.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was this interview conducted in a question and answer format? In other words, the investigators asked questions and you provided answers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, do you have an objection to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the question should be Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. asked, "How was the interview conducted?" as you yourself indicated to us. My objection is the same as the one raised in respect of the anarchical manner in which the changeover was carried out, and I should also like to restrict my -- my learned colleague restrict himself to the areas that were covered in the cross-examination and not lead any new evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe it's generally accepted that, with respect to foundational questions, it's a little bit of leeway with respect to the form of the question, whether it's considered a leading or direct question. Therefore, I'm simply trying to get to the foundation of the statement and then there will be particular questions. Since the statement was utilised by every counsel, I'm simply trying to clear up some matters with respect to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think that we agreed that, as regards general questions, they can be formulated in a different manner. However, since this is a very sensitive issue for the Defence, let us make an exception to the rule. Could you please rephrase your question, Mr. Keegan, so that you avoid any inferences, any conclusions, just because this is a very sensitive issue for the Defence. If you could please do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. For the record then, I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Witness J, how was the interview conducted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was answering questions that were put to me by the investigators who were conducting the interview, and it was a normal conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And during this time in February of 1995, did you find it -- well, what was your state of mind with respect to sitting through a long interview with regards to all of the events which happened to you in 1992? Was it easy, was it difficult?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is always difficult for me to talk about that. It's perfectly normal, I think. I have certain emotions about that, and it's a perfectly normal reaction. But the people who talked to me were very relaxed, calm, normal. Nobody insisted on my talking about the things I didn't wish to talk about, and never at any point in time did I feel under any pressure. People listened to what I was telling them and only to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Investigators did not press you on answers that you gave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: They were typing the answers as you gave them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right away. I was able to control what was being recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was this interview process a difficult or tiring experience or did you find it easy to deal with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already told you, one always has certain emotional reactions in such situations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection to the question put by Mr. Keegan. The witness has already told us that the conversation was a relaxed one. So I think that this question now points to something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm happy to leave it to the record and for conclusions to the Court, but I believe she said that she found it extremely difficult but that the investigators were relaxed. I'm happy to leave the record as it stands.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Normal." I said "normal," as far as I can follow the discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is good. I think this is the good conclusion; that is to say, you should leave the conclusions to the Chamber. If the witness has said that it had been a difficult experience for her, the Chamber is going to read the transcript. It is not necessary to repeat. So it is similar to the question that we already had if the changeover of the guards was carried out in an anarchical manner or not. You make allegations and we will make conclusions, but please, it is not upon the parties to draw conclusions. Please restrict yourselves to questions, and please formulate your questions in a clear, specific, and concise manner. Clear, specific, and concise. This is a very sensitive issue again, Mr. Keegan, and we have to be very careful. We should not be drawing conclusions, and one should not leave the witness to draw conclusions but let the witness speak in a spontaneous manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I could have the assistance of the usher again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Witness J, yesterday Mr. Simic read selected sentences or passages from the statement. I would now like to ask you some follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If we could put the English version on the ELMO, please, so that the Court can see the full paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yesterday -- and we're talking now on page 5 of your statement. Yesterday, Mr. Simic asked you some questions about Mr. Meakic and specifically referred to one paragraph on page 5 and referred to one sentence where he indicated that you had said Mr. Meakic told a guard that he could not drink. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Go down, please. Or move the sheet up. Move it up. Move it up. There.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Now, the guard -- this is on page 4 in the Bosnian. The guard in question, the one who bothered Namka, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Namka Alisic. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That guard who was on duty upstairs in the hallway, the guard that you referred to, who would be on duty upstairs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would come from time to time, but it was not his regular duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see guards drinking in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And how often did that occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Now if we could go to page 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Page 5. Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you also state in that statement that while you did not see Zeljko Meakic himself commit crimes, you did see him present when crimes were being committed against prisoners, and you saw him walk past dead bodies. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday, we dwelled on these issues with the witness for some time concerning Mr. Kvocka, Mr. Prcac, and Mr. Krkan, and the witness was clear enough. Mr. Meakic was not mentioned at all in the cross-examination, and the topic is being widened here, and if I may say so, it is not relevant to the case because Mr. Meakic is not here. This portion of the statement was not used at all, the portion of the statement that Mr. Keegan is now referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm happy to pull the transcript right now and settle this. I know the Court is reluctant to refer back to the transcript, which is why I responded to Mr. Nikolic's objection the way I did, but the question was specifically asked yesterday about Mr. Meakic and about whether he issued orders to tell the guard he could not drink on duty, the inference being, of course, that her testimony with respect to that Meakic was present when crimes were being committed was inconsistent with her prior statement, and I'm simply attempting to show that, in fact, she was consistent in her statement with her testimony, and there are further passages that I'm going to get to with respect to Mr. Kvocka and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I reply, Your Honour? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection is rejected. Mr. Keegan, please proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now, if the usher could move it down just slightly so the paragraph which you can just see on the ELMO, you can see the full paragraph, please. Right there. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Witness J, yesterday Mr. Simic read just a selected portion on page 5, and he asked you about the question about whether you had said in your statement that Mr. Meakic was always present in the camp. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: But did you also say in your statement, some three paragraphs later, speaking about Mr. Kvocka, the accused, that when Zeljko was not in the camp, those who needed to go see the commander went to Miroslav?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If we could go to page 9, please. Page 9. Right there. That's good, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Again, referring to Mr. Simic's questions, yesterday he asked you about a man named Mirko Babic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And he asked you questions about whether Mirko Babic had told you that he was an engineer. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And he asked you questions regarding Mirko Babic's position before the war as a member of the staff at the Omarska mining complex. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: He also asked you if Mr. Babic wore civilian clothes. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: But did you also say in your statement, which was not read to you, that Mr. Babic sometimes wore a police uniform; he sometimes wore civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That he would come to your sleeping room in the evening and tell you that someone had to go to Separacija the next day and clean there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And with respect to his work obligation, which was also a question raised, you were asked if Mr. Babic told you that his obligation was to ensure the mine continued as normal. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And did you not also say in your statement in 1995 that, in response to that, you thought that was odd since the mine was now a camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was no logic in it, for it to start working, because all the premises and the whole space was full of prisoners, so that was rather funny.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Witness J, did Mirko Babic call women out of the rooms at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did any of those women ever tell you what happened when Mirko Babic called them out of the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I'd like to move on now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You can take the statement, thank you. I'd like to move on now to this issue of the newspaper article referred to, the article by the French press agency. Could I ask the witness to be provided the copy of the newspaper article, please. I'm referring to the Defence exhibit. Not that one, the Defence exhibit. The D31/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You have a version there in your own language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I just want to ask you a few questions about this article. Witness J, were you shown the contents of this article by the reporter prior to its publication?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, objection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this for the first time yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Objection overruled. I think we ought to hear the answer to the question. What is your objection, Mr. Krstan Simic? No, now I want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wanted to object before the answer to the question was given because quite obviously the Prosecution is leading -- or misleading the witness, and we said a moment ago that this was an interview. We got the document from the Prosecution, and we are surprised to see that they did not analyse it. This is a statement from what Witness J said at a press conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, this was the object of several questions in the cross-examination. Even if it was a document furnished by the Prosecution, the Prosecution can conduct all kinds of analyses; but here in the courtroom, as the Defence always defended the question and we always discussed all preliminary declarations, the defence took the stand that what we -- what counted was what is said orally in the courtroom. So what counts is what's stated orally in the courtroom. So independent of all the analyses the Prosecution did before, he is asking it for the first time here in the courtroom, so I overrule the objection, and I ask Mr. Keegan to continue. And please bear in mind one thing: Do not lead the witness into giving an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. I just want to clarify. I believe we did get the answer to the question on the record. I won't repeat it if we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Witness J, were you shown the contents of this article by the reporter prior to its publication?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said, and I repeat, I saw this article for the first time yesterday when it was shown to me by the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Witness J, were you at any time asked to confirm the details or the facts contained -- the alleged facts which are contained in that article, either by the reporter or by the press agency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you asked at any time to confirm whether you had, in fact, made the statements that are attributed to you in that article by the reporter or by the press agency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The conference which you were attending at the time, how was it that you came to be at that conference? Why were you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered a question put to me by the Defence counsel yesterday. He mentioned some committee of survivors, or whatever it was called, that I attended the conference as part of a delegation of the women of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is a non-governmental organisation, a women's organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And was that non-governmental organisation, that NGO, invited to send a delegation to that conference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And several of us went, not only myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were members of that delegation asked to give press conferences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were. Not only by that organisation, but several organisations held press conferences on that particular day, the ones that were present at the conference. So it was not only me that talked about this, but other former prisoners as well, female ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Now, with respect to this issue about the changing of the shifts and the assignment of guards, how is it that you are aware that assignments were on occasion given to guards inside the building, that is, up in the office which you referred to? How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went upstairs and would come back, and they talked about it, who they had to report to, the commander, the deputy, prior to a shift. This wasn't something that was kept secret. They talked about it openly in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who is "they" that you refer to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guards, the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you able to see or to observe how the guards -- how different guards arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: This was fully canvassed on direct examination, and counsel had the opportunity to put these questions at that time to his witness. My submission is he's attempting to reopen direct examination. And when he had the opportunity to do so on direct, he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. O'Sullivan, let's hear the question. I don't know whether you know, and I don't know if Mr. Keegan is going to set the frameworks for a question or not, or what he's going to do. So shall we wait and see what he's actually going to do? We have understood the gist of your objection, but I'm going to ask Mr. Keegan to continue with his questioning to see whether it is an isolated question or laying the foundations for something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Without going into the specifics, the point of this is the Defence asked a number of questions on this. We think that there is a particular reason why they were focussed in that direction, to try and perhaps show consistencies either with this witness or others. Of course, we all come from different jurisdictions here. Mr. O'Sullivan comes from one where redirect is extremely limited; however, we don't believe that the practice before this Tribunal, the jurisprudence before this Tribunal, indicates --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Keegan, I apologise for interrupting you. The Chamber understands. Go ahead with your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Witness J, I'll repeat the question. Were you able to see or to observe how different guards arrived at the camp for their shifts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean, how they arrived at the camp? Could you clarify that, please? You mean what brought them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mode they came there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How they arrived at the camp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came by bus usually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And after the bus arrived, would the shift that was leaving leave on that bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: To your knowledge -- let me ask it this way. You've talked about the guards going upstairs to get assignments and then talking about it. Did that always occur at the same time of day, or would it occur throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually in the morning when they came to work, usually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Now with respect to the questions asked by Mr. Masic, you referred to the list when you were called out by Mr. Prcac, when you were being transferred to the Trnopolje camp. Did you have an opportunity to see that list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were standing in a semicircle. Prcac was holding the list. (redacted), she was sitting down like this with her head on her hands, and I said, "Why don't you get up? We're going." And she said, "There's a minus sign next to my name. I'll never leave this place." And that was Velida Mahmuljin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did Velida Mahmuljin leave the camp with you that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Nothing has been heard of her up until the present day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were there any other names --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Keegan. A question was asked: "Velida Mahmuljin, did she leave the place with you or not?" I'd like to have the witness's answer. Could you repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Witness J, did Velida Mahmuljin leave the camp with you on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: She did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, has she ever been seen again since that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never up until the present day. Nothing is known about Velida.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were there other women in your group that day --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: -- who also did not leave the camp with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mugbila Besirevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, has anything been heard or has she ever been seen since that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the present day, nothing has ever been heard of her, about her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no questions. That's not what I wanted to take the floor about. You told us that these are witnesses of the Court and that it is our job here to ascertain the truth. Did we hear here -- and when the Defence showed the interview by Agence France Presse, and when the Prosecutor at the end showed that article to the witness, did -- we'd like to have an answer. Did the witness say what it said in the France Presse article or not? Does it say something that the witness did not state or does it not? That is the crux of the question. I apologise for raising it again, but I really do think the answer is crucial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. Fila. We're not going to open up a discussion on that. It is true that the witness said that she saw the document for the first time yesterday when it was shown to her by the Defence counsel, and we can't oblige the witness to say anything else. That is what the witness said, and that's what we have to accept. We have to accept what we hear. I am very sorry, Mr. Fila, but we can't open up that discussion again. You can take the point up in your defence, in your final statements and so on, but not have it argumented here. Now we come to the Judges' question. We might go beyond our time limit before the break, we might go beyond 11.00, so perhaps it would be better to take a break now before the Judges ask their questions. We said beforehand that the room is very hot and that it's almost becoming a sauna. We might need a cold shower and give the witness a chance to have a rest. So we're going to have a half-hour break. Would the usher please lower the blinds to allow the witness to leave the courtroom escorted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We reconvene round about 11.25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Let us resume with the questions of the Chamber. Judge Riad has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness J, I can't call you by your name, so good morning. I would appreciate your shedding some more light on a few points if you are in a position to do so and even if you have referred to some of them before in passing. I have at least one or two global questions, one concerning the command of the camp. There was the official command, there was the camp commanders, yes, it was Kvocka and -- then Meakic, then Kvocka, then Prcac, and there were the shift commanders, Krkan, Ckalja, and Krle. Was there some kind of conflict between these commanders or was this command coinciding with one another? Was it the same policy and completed one another? Who was in full control, the camp commanders or the shift commanders, in your opinion or your assessment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me first answer the first part of your question. I didn't see any conflict break out between them at any point in time. They were cooperating all the time. They were doing the work together, completing one another, as far as I could observe, and on the basis of that, I can reach this conclusion. That is because I saw that during my stay in the camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You said cooperation. Was there a certain hierarchy, or were they on equal footing in practice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I noticed was cooperation, a complete cooperation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, when there was a commander like Kvocka and then a commander like Prcac, was there a difference in the camp atmosphere, in the treatment of the detainees, or was the difference according to the shift commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: The atmosphere was more or less the same. It was quite similar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And according to the shift, to the shifts, was the atmosphere the same in all shifts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to what I saw, it seems to me that the worst atmosphere was the one led by Mladjo Radic, called Krkan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: When you say worst, was it that nobody would stop, nobody would stop the guards from doing anything, and on other shifts they would be stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that doesn't mean that. I personally remember the guards from Krkan's shift, from the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And why do you remember them in particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they beat the detainees who came there to get their meal, because they would shout at them, and because of the one who used to abuse us women, verbally in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And was Krkan around with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would come to the restaurant very often.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And he would not stop anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did any of the commanders, shift commanders or camp commanders, give, to your knowledge, orders to beat or to mistreat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear or see him do that in my presence, orders to beat people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did any of the commanders you have seen during the period give orders not to beat or prevent it? You gave only one example of Meakic who asked the guard to report to him because he was drunk and bothered, bothered Namka. Was that the only instance you saw of a commander interfering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw anyone prevent any incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: With this incident of Meakic, what was the reaction of the guard when Meakic called him to order? Did he obey? Did you notice that there was a real discipline when somebody -- when a commander interfered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he continued coming to our room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So he continued, but the order was obeyed? Any order would be obeyed when you were watching?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But the camp was functioning with regularity and discipline?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: The camp was functioning, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So there was discipline?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that there was discipline because tortures were an everyday occurrence, and nobody prevented anyone from doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Torture could be part of the discipline and could be the result of guards doing anything they wanted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my impression.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the tortures went on, that they could do as they pleased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The guards were free to do as they pleased?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my conclusion, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, if you look at the lists, when somebody came and read the lists, there was always a list according to which detainees were called, or could the guards call anyone they wanted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could call out anyone they wanted, any of the detainees, even without the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Those who never came back, were they usually on the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. lists, or called by any guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could be on the list, but they could also be called out without the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You had an opportunity to see a list. When you went in the room, you had a glance. What is your memory of it? Was it some kind of official list coming from an official place, or handwritten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how it was, but I could clearly see the name that I mentioned at the beginning of my testimony. The names of detainees were on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I was afraid. The list scared me, actually, and I wanted to get rid of it as soon as possible. I wanted to hand it over. And I saw a name. It was the name of the former mayor of the Prijedor municipality, Mr. Muhamed Cehajic. The name was underlined in red pencil, and next to his name...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Are you finished?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You said, "And next to his name," and you stopped.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word "again," the word "again," "ponovo," was standing next to it, and I could conclude from that that he was to be interrogated again. I don't know whether my conclusion was right or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was this just handwritten or lists -- official lists coming?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Handwritten next to the name in red pencil.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But the lists themselves, could you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that I don't remember, but I think, I think that it was typed out, the list itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was there a typewriter in the office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which office do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The one where you saw, the one where you saw the list.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: The list was found in the room where we would spend the night after we had completed our work in the restaurant, and that is where the investigators carried out the interrogations of the detainees, and my assumption is that they had left the list in the room, that they didn't put it away after they had finished their work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did you see, since you have been cleaning sometimes, did you see any of the commanders typing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And this list, you mentioned the mayor of Prijedor. Who were the people usually called on these lists? What category of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were members of political parties, including the Party of Democratic Action and the Croatian Democratic Union, individuals who held very high positions, used to work as highly-ranking public servants, people who were well off, respected members of the community.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You mentioned two ladies, Velida and Mugbila, who were the ones on the list with the mark. She told you that her name had a minor mark. Was she part of any big political gathering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Velida Mahmuljin, as far as I know, was a member of the Party of Democratic Action, and she used to live in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did they openly accuse her of anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: She said that they had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of her membership in that political party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask you about Mr. Krkan's attitude with you. You said -- I won't repeat it, when he molested you, but offered to come to you at night for eventual intercourse, with a mattress, and offered you, apparently, to put you in a better category. Was this accompanied by any threat if you didn't, or he just spoke of the reward?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: He spoke about the reward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So he was, in your opinion, in a position to save you, to save anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did you notice this done with other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Could you just tell me "yes" means that they saved them? What happened exactly? Could these commanders change the fate of anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they could change the fate of people to a great extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And stop the guards from doing anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Just a last question. Just I want to visualise this hosing down the detainees, this bath they gave them, because was this the daily bath for the detainees or was it some kind of entertainment? What was it exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The way it was undertaken, how was it done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me, it looked like they were having fun with it, but actually, it was a very painful sight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Could you just tell me how painful?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was difficult for me to watch them as to how those who were being hosed down were feeling. I can only imagine. People stumbled down because of the heavy jet of water. They were falling down to the ground. They were completely naked. Amongst the men there was a woman, Hajra Hadzic, as I said at the beginning of my testimony. That woman was in the "white house" all the time, and she never left the camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And were women mistreated the same way as men exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't bathe us with that hose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But apart from that, as far as beating is concerned and going to the restaurant and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in front of me. I never saw a woman being beaten up, with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What about the two minors? You said there were two minors. How old were they and how were they treated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as all other male detainees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: How old were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below the age of 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness J, thank you very much, and I apologise for having been too long. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Riad. Madam Judge Wald has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Witness J, I believe you testified that when you went to clean the rooms where the interrogations had gone on, you, on occasion, would see signs of blood and sometimes signs of torn clothing, and I think you also testified that sometimes when you were downstairs in the restaurant, you could hear sounds of blows or cries coming from the interrogation rooms upstairs.
